status: problem-boundary ledger with finite diagnostic witnesses; not a proof of four-dimensional Yang-Mills existence or a mass gap

clayProblem.gaugeGroups: every compact simple gauge group G
clayProblem.existence: construct a nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills theory with axiomatic properties at least as strong as the cited Wightman and Osterwalder-Schrader frameworks
clayProblem.massGap: for the Hamiltonian H with vacuum energy zero, there is Delta>0 such that spec(H) has no support in (0,Delta), with finite maximal gap
clayProblem.localContent: gauge-invariant local operators corresponding to renormalized polynomials in F and its covariant derivatives, with short-distance behavior consistent with asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization

minkowskiRequirements: unitary Poincare covariance and positive-energy spectrum
a unique Poincare-invariant vacuum up to phase
tempered/operator-valued distribution control adequate for reconstruction
euclideanRequirements: continuum Schwinger functions whose reconstruction gives the physical Hilbert space and Hamiltonian
reconstructionGate.warning: a gauge-fixed propagator or positive numerical correlator is not by itself an Osterwalder-Schrader construction

logicalSeparations.spectralGap: a statement about the physical Hamiltonian spectrum above the vacuum
logicalSeparations.confinement: a distinct statement about color/non-singlet states or large Wilson-loop behavior; neither definition alone automatically proves the other in the required continuum theory
logicalSeparations.higgsMass: a mass generated after adding a Higgs sector is not the pure quantum Yang-Mills mass-gap result
logicalSeparations.finiteLattice: a lowest excitation at fixed lattice spacing and finite volume does not prove a positive gap uniform in volume and nonzero after continuum scaling
logicalSeparations.perturbativeMass: ordinary perturbation theory about the trivial vacuum does not generate the required gauge-invariant infrared spectrum

oneLoopDimensionalTransmutationWitness.meaning: the one-loop RG invariant supplies a scale but does not prove existence, positivity, confinement, or a mass gap

strongCouplingWitness.model: four-dimensional SU(2) Wilson lattice action, leading fundamental character-expansion term
strongCouplingWitness.meaning: this is a controlled leading strong-coupling lattice witness, not the weak-coupling continuum limit required by Clay

correlationGapWitness.meaning: exponential decay can diagnose a supplied positive transfer-matrix spectrum; fitting it does not construct the continuum theory or prove a volume- and cutoff-uniform gap

spin23Boundary.groupFact: Spin(2,3) is noncompact, whereas the Clay statement is for compact simple G
spin23Boundary.sharedComplexification: spin(2,3) and compact spin(5) are real forms of so(5,C)
spin23Boundary.positivityObstruction: complexification does not transport reflection positivity, a positive Hilbert space, or a spectral gap between real forms
spin23Boundary.gravityConstraint: a universal gap for the full Spin(2,3) connection would conflict with the required long-range massless spin-2 sector
spin23Boundary.admissibleTarget: retain a massless Einstein graviton while proving positive physical spectral support only for non-Einstein torsion/coset/auxiliary sectors; keep compact internal Yang-Mills as a separate factor
spin23Boundary.nonPromotion: the group name, symmetry breaking, or a shared complexified algebra does not solve the compact Yang-Mills problem

nextGates: write the exact gauge-invariant Euclidean measure or controlled regulator and specify the observable algebra
prove reflection positivity and a positive transfer matrix before interpreting exponential decay as mass
establish thermodynamic-limit Schwinger functions and clustering uniformly in finite volume
construct a renormalized continuum trajectory with asymptotic-freedom short-distance behavior
prove a lower spectral bound uniform in volume and cutoff whose physical-unit limit is nonzero
show nontriviality and regulator universality rather than a Gaussian or lattice-artifact limit
separate and independently test mass gap, Wilson-loop confinement, center symmetry, and glueball pole claims
for the Spin(2,3) programme, derive the quadratic spectrum and BRST/constraint cohomology and isolate the massless spin-2 pole
test a compact Spin(5) lattice proxy, then either prove a positivity-preserving bridge to the intended real form or record a no-go
derive any relation between an internal Yang-Mills scale, the Spin(2,3)-breaking scale, and the cosmological scale rather than identifying them by notation
decision: No present Spin(2,3) construction solves the four-dimensional compact Yang-Mills existence-and-gap problem. The useful programme is a typed sequence of positivity, limit, spectrum, and sector-separation gates with finite calculations retained only as regression witnesses.
